finding.title: Wrap DeviceRegistryDatabase.removeAccount's delete + state-clear in a transaction()

evidence.quote:
for (var i = 1; i < group.length; i++) {
        removed += await removeAccount(group[i].accountId);

finding.why: removeAccount's own docstring says it clears lastActiveAccountId 'so the next launch does NOT silently auto-activate an arbitrary fallback account against a dangling pointer (D10)' — but the delete and the pointer-clear are two separately-awaited statements with no db.transaction() around them. If the process dies between them (routine on Android when a backgrounded app is reclaimed, and account removal is exactly the kind of action a user triggers then backgrounds), the delete commits but the clear never runs, leaving deviceState.lastActiveAccountId pointing at a row that no longer exists — the exact D10 state device_registry_test.dart's 'removeAccount clears it when removing the ACTIVE account (D10)' test checks for, just reached through a crash path the in-memory test can't simulate. dedupeByEmail compounds this by calling removeAccount N times in an unwrapped loop, so a mid-run crash also leaves a partially-merged duplicate-account state. Every other multi-write DAO in this codebase (stage_dao.dart, curriculum_scope_dao.dart, user_profile_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart) wraps its writes in transaction() — this file is the outlier.
finding.recommendation: Wrap removeAccount's body in `await transaction(() async { ... })`; wrap dedupeByEmail's per-group removal loop in one enclosing transaction (or a single batched delete) so a crash mid-merge can't leave a partially-deduped state.
acceptance_criteria: removeAccount and dedupeByEmail are wrapped in transaction()/batch(); a new test forces an exception between the delete and the state-clear and asserts neither write applied.
DB-2's Pending checker (audit grep for ≥2 awaited writes with no enclosing transaction() in a DAO method body) returns zero for this file.
